target_customer: Commercial fleet operators and truck OEMs paying for diesel and range savings
problem: Truck speed management wastes diesel and electric range. Hypermile Co-Pilot is a retrofittable AI cruise control that anticipates traffic and road gradient, and began as a driver coach.
business_model: Hardware plus software subscription for fleets, with OEM integration ambitions
product_category: AI driver assistance and cruise control for trucks

founders.name: James Hennessey
education: UCL, PhD in computer vision and graphics
founders.background_notes: Entrepreneur First alum per the YC page. Another source also credits him with CTO.

founders.name: Jakub Langr
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as a former founder.

technical_complexity.rationale: Predictive speed control using CAN bus integration, sensors and models for trucks needs embedded and ML work plus safety validation for a tiny team.

defensibility.rationale: Integration with vehicle systems and driving data is harder than software alone, but OEM cruise control and fleet telematics players could build similar features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copy found in sources. The YC status is Acquired with no acquirer named; a low authority aggregator names K1 in May 2024.

market_need_then: Diesel is a top fleet cost and EU and UK emission rules and trucking electrification raised the value of efficiency and range. Innovate UK and Department for Transport grants backed the work.

branding.domain_note: Current hypermile.ai site presents a product made by Konboi, so the domain or brand appears to have passed to another company.

identity.logo: white square mark per file name, not verified
identity.visual_style: Large headline statistics and short taglines
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and forward looking; tagline Superhuman AI Cruise Control

brand_strength.rationale: The name plays on the existing hypermiling term which helps meaning but is hard to own; no press about the brand and no community found.

pivots.from: Driver coaching platform for diesel and electric trucks
pivots.to: Retrofittable AI cruise control with a Level 3 autonomy goal
pivots.why: Not sourced; inferred from the Catapult project summary versus the later YC description, treat as unverified

outcome_analysis: Hypermile was a London team of about ten that built an AI speed controller for trucks, backed by YC and UK government grants. It claimed 11 percent diesel savings and independent project data showed about 6.8 percent fuel savings against an experienced driver. The sources do not show large venture rounds and the YC status is Acquired with no public buyer or terms, so the story reads as a small grant funded hardware software company that exited quietly.
notes: The YC page claims a 1.5M pre-seed in May 2021 led by YC with Greg Brockman and Luc Vincent; CB Insights lists only 540K total (Startup Autobahn, Innovate UK, YC), so the amount is unverified and left null. Acquirer K1 in May 2024 appears only on BounceWatch and is unverified. The hypermile.ai site is branded by Konboi and mentions no acquisition. Competitor sources found (PedalCoach, Isaac Coach, Blue Tree) date from 2016 to 2018, outside the batch window, so none are listed. Batch says Summer 2020 while founded 2020 per YC. Pivot row is inference and unverified.
